decisions.reason: Underside maintenance access does not necessarily change the platform's configuration, height, cup clearance, or mixer fit.
The sanitation-access clause is a separate requirement concern and already has its own same-message MODIFY; underside serviceability adds no change to the sanitary fluid-path state.
The maintenance-access decision does not alter any machine, platform, font, or button color requirement.
Underside serviceability has no necessary effect on branding text, placard placement, logo treatment, or display sides.
Access beneath the machine for maintenance is distinct from bowl removal, swapping, and cleaning clearance, which remain unchanged.
The maintenance-access addition does not change the V1 speed priority or off-the-shelf versus custom-fabrication sourcing policy.
The source retains the integrated product appearance and does not modify the DJ-turntable-inspired visual identity.
Underside maintenance access does not alter bowl depth, capacity, or the accepted bowl-size reference.
The message reiterates concern about high-RPM splash control but establishes no new splash target or mitigation beyond the candidate's existing state.
Praise for the curved spout and plumbing integration does not change the required spout geometry, orientation, construction, or pour direction.
The progress observation about physical integration does not modify the system-layout or CAD deliverable.
The underside-access requirement does not change the approved component set, BOM obligations, or component-selection criteria.
